findings.source_passage: For blacks, the year's calendar should show naught but three hundred and sixty-five Fourth of Julys and New Year's Days.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a rhetorically distinctive and interpretively significant line — ironic, pointed commentary on race and festivity that critics frequently cite; its erasure removes a key register marker in Melville's treatment of Pip.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim within the Pip character introduction paragraph.

findings.source_passage: behold yon lustrous ebony, panelled in king's cabinets
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, after 'even blackness has its brilliancy'
findings.why_it_matters: The appositive image anchors the diamond/ebony extended metaphor that follows; without it the jeweller conceit loses its grounding in racial beauty and the rhetorical force of the passage is diminished.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the clause after 'even blackness has its brilliancy; behold yon lustrous ebony, panelled in king's cabinets.'

findings.source_passage: with his gay ha-ha! had turned the round horizon into one star-belled tambourine
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, end of Pip's Connecticut description
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most prosodically distinctive phrases in the chapter — the tambourine motif closure and the image of the round horizon-as-tambourine are critically noted as structuring Pip's symbolic identity; their loss flattens the voice materially.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Connecticut/fiddler's frolic passage including 'gay ha-ha!' and 'round horizon into one star-belled tambourine.'

findings.source_passage: It was a beautiful, bounteous, blue day; the spangled sea calm and cool, and flatly stretching away, all round, to the horizon, like gold-beater's skin hammered out to the extremest.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after second jump, description of sea
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses 'beautiful, bounteous, blue' to a bare 'bright, blue day' and loses 'spangled sea calm and cool' — the alliterative, rhythmic texture that makes the passage's cruel beauty palpable is diminished.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the alliterative opening 'beautiful, bounteous, blue day; the spangled sea calm and cool' and the full gold-beater's skin simile.

summary: Three medium-severity signature losses — the 365 Fourth of Julys line, the lustrous ebony image, and the star-belled tambourine phrase — collectively erase the most critically noticed passages in Pip's character introduction and trigger regeneration.
